TITLE: Q3 2024 Company-Wide Status Report  

**Summary**  
Zastama Industries continues to make steady progress across its key initiatives, driven by focused efforts in product development, research, and operational security. This report outlines recent achievements, ongoing priorities, and potential areas for attention. The cross-functional collaboration between teams remains a cornerstone of our success, and we remain committed to aligning our efforts with long-term strategic goals.  

**Progress**  
Pikera Tasfeis has led the Product team in refining our internal payments reconciliation tools, which are now in the final stages of internal testing. These tools are expected to significantly reduce manual effort and improve the accuracy of financial reporting. Her work also includes engaging with the finance lead to ensure alignment with the broader financial systems architecture. Pikera Tasfeis continues to focus on payments reconciliation, and her contributions have already begun to streamline workflows across multiple departments.  

Porpean Tudima, as Head of Security, has prioritized customer onboarding flows, implementing stronger authentication protocols and data-privacy safeguards. These enhancements are in direct response to recent industry trends and regulatory changes. Porpean Tudima focuses on customer onboarding flows, and recent workshops with the compliance and engineering teams have ensured that these updates will not disrupt the user experience. The Security team has also completed a company-wide audit of access controls, which has identified a number of areas for improvement.  

In the Daslaor Applied Research Lab, Zodoine Vemdaen is investigating new methods for predictive modeling in supply chain optimization. This work is part of a larger initiative to integrate advanced analytics into our logistics and procurement systems. Zodoine Vemdaen is a member of the Daslaor Applied Research Lab and continues to collaborate with stakeholders in operations and vendor management to define the scope and impact of these models. The lab is also exploring opportunities for external collaboration, while remaining focused on internally driven innovation.  

Stethe Birnaen, who joined the company in 2016, continues to contribute to the development of machine learning tools for internal forecasting. A recent project led by Stethe Birnaen works as a Data Scientist has resulted in the successful deployment of a new demand-prediction model, which is now being used to support inventory planning. Stethe Birnaen has also been working closely with the Product and Engineering teams to ensure seamless integration of data tools with our existing platforms.  

**Risks**  
While progress is being made across departments, there are a few key risks to remain mindful of. The rollout of the new customer onboarding tools, led by Porpean Tudima, requires careful coordination to avoid disruptions to new account setups. Any misalignment between the new flows and legacy systems could lead to delays in user activation, which could impact customer satisfaction.  

Pikera Tasfeis is working to ensure that the payments reconciliation tools are fully compatible with our external vendors, and while integration is progressing well, there is a risk of delayed adoption if training and documentation are not completed on time.  

In the Daslaor Applied Research Lab, Zodoine Vemdaen is navigating the challenge of balancing exploratory research with the need for practical, near-term outcomes. The lab must continue to demonstrate the value of its work in measurable, business-focused terms.  

Stethe Birnaen, despite his long tenure and strong track record, is also facing the challenge of ensuring that the machine learning models he develops are fully understood and trusted by non-technical stakeholders. Continued communication and training will be key to maintaining buy-in and effective implementation.  

**Next Steps**  
In the coming weeks, several key actions will be prioritized across the organization. Pikera Tasfeis will lead the final rollout of the payments reconciliation tools, with a focus on user training and support. A company-wide session is planned for early December to introduce the new system and address any questions.  

Porpean Tudima will begin a phased deployment of the updated customer onboarding flows, starting with a small group of new accounts to test the system’s performance. The Security team will also initiate a review of access policies to ensure that permissions are aligned with current roles and responsibilities.  

Zodoine Vemdaen will present the findings of the latest research project to the executive leadership team in December. This presentation will include a roadmap for how the proposed models can be scaled and integrated into production systems.  

Stethe Birnaen will begin work on a new initiative to improve data quality across the company, and he will be reaching out to department leads to gather requirements and define success metrics.  

Finally, the company will continue to emphasize cross-departmental communication and collaboration. We encourage all employees to remain engaged, share feedback, and stay informed of ongoing developments through regular team meetings and internal updates.  

We appreciate the continued dedication of every team member and look forward to a productive end to the year.
